rep.name: Michael Brideau
rep.location: Medellín, Colombia — about to relocate to Brazil; Canadian

prospect.name: Tom Eldon
prospect.location: Saco, Maine, USA — 15 to 20 minutes south of Portland, on the coast; resident 16 years
prospect.occupation: Retired. 32 years at UPS as a delivery driver, walking five to ten miles a day, five or six days a week; retired May 2025. Currently building a shed roughly two days a week for a friend as repayment for managing his 401k.
prospect.family_status: Single and cooking for himself; previously married, 'I did my 14 years with that.' No children mentioned. Tight group of travelling surf friends, notably Dan, 71, a retired UPS colleague who manages his 401k and sets his competitive benchmark.
prospect.training_background: Very active and highly self-directed, 17 consecutive weeks of consistent training and the first sustained programme of his life. Four to five days a week: roughly 45 minutes of Michael Holland's lymphatic-drainage Tai Chi, about 30 minutes of kettlebell work, then walking four to twelve miles a day, averaging 137 miles a month across May and June. Adds reverse hill climbs, which he credits with resolving a meniscus problem, and three to five sets of thirty push-ups on an outdoor loop. Refuses gyms — 'I hate the gym, you'll never catch me in a gym.' Surfs, hikes 4,000-footers, snowshoes, skates and mountain bikes. Travelled four and a half months out of the last twelve.
prospect.medical: Atrial fibrillation and what he called 'STV' (apparently SVT), surgically repaired; still registers AFib around 2% of the time or less on his Apple Watch, which he describes as not debilitating and not affecting training. Surgically repaired torn Achilles on the left side, with persistent and probably permanent calf atrophy — 'the calf is noticeably smaller on that side... I don't think it'll ever come back to match the other side.' Shattered left radius mountain biking in Colorado in 2018, repaired. Meniscus problem that stopped him descending a mountain last summer, which he believes he has self-rehabilitated. Intermittent pain in both knees. Following a month ago he found Trevor via reels. On no medications.

signals: Older, retired and explicitly optimising for holding on to capability rather than acquiring anything: 'my goal is longevity, at this point in my life... I just want to keep doing the things I love to do. like surf and hike and for as long as I can'

Health-literate and already medically managed — cardiac ablation for AFib and SVT, surgical Achilles and radius repairs, tracks sleep scores, scans groceries with the Yuka app, self-rehabilitated a meniscus with reverse hill climbs

The classic preserver financial shape: nominally comfortable, functionally illiquid. 'I've got money to cover everything' sits alongside 'I'm on a fixed income now', a pension, newly started social security and a 401k, with the $6,000 weighed directly against booked travel

Frames the purchase as insurance against injury rather than as gain: 'my concern is, I really like it, and I want to go forward with it, but I don't want to hurt myself, you know, that would be devastating'
Not the_rebuilder: he has lost no ground and is arguably in the best condition of his adult life after 17 unbroken weeks; he is defending a position, not recovering one

goals.text: Longevity — keep surfing, hiking, snowshoeing and skating for as long as possible, ideally into his eighties
Athleticism and performance for surfing specifically — 'All I care about is performance, you know, what I can do when I'm out there'
Build core and hip strength, which he identifies as the weak link in his surfing
Learn correct kettlebell technique so he does not injure himself — the stated reason for seeking coaching at all
Get in the best shape of his life now that retirement has freed up the time
Lose the lower-back and love-handle fat that he has not been able to shift
Keep up with Dan, his 71-year-old surfing friend who out-performs him — 'there's a little competitiveness there. So if I can get an edge, sure, I'll take it'
Redirect the energy that went into 32 years at UPS back into himself

pains.text: Fear of injuring himself through incorrect kettlebell technique — the single most-repeated concern on the call: 'I just don't want to get hurt doing it'
Four and a half months of travel in a twelve-month span makes a consistent routine impossible — 'you can't carry kettlebells with you', and he names this as what has delayed the decision
No structure or plan behind his nutrition — 'I don't really have anything structured that I follow. I just try to do the best I can while I'm at the grocery store'
Weak core and hips limiting surfing performance
Permanent calf atrophy on the surgically repaired left side that a year of hard work has barely changed
Residual atrial fibrillation post-surgery, which he monitors on a watch and treats as a non-issue
Intermittent bilateral knee pain and a meniscus problem that stopped him getting off a mountain last summer
The last few years at UPS were physically punishing — 'It was physically painful just to get up and go to work every day'
Retirement income is newly configured and not yet understood — a pension, just-started social security and a 401k that he has not reconciled against his travel commitments
Occasional broken sleep, roughly once every two or three weeks, where he wakes and cannot get back down

objections.raw_quote: Oh yeah. I mean, if, yeah, if the price is right, sure. You know? Okay. I, I, it, you know, I'm on a fixed income now.
objections.rep_response: Pre-empted the price with the fixed-income caveat already on the table and quoted $6,000 immediately without addressing it. Later isolated it properly — 'finances aside, like it does kind of check all the boxes for you... Correct?' — and ran a genuine ability-versus-uncertainty diagnostic: 'is it more a matter of like, hey, actually, it's just tight, and I probably couldn't actually do $6,000 right now? Or is it more, there's maybe a little bit of like, kind of uncertainty around, do I actually spend the $6,000?'

objections.raw_quote: That's a big investment. But I mean, I understand the effects of it and all that. It's just a matter of whether it's the right fit for me at this point in my life. I, yeah, I would have to take some time and think about that one.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without running any of the scripted deliberation play. Said 'Okay. Yeah. Not an issue' and moved to isolate the finances instead. When it returned at the end as a hard 24-hour requirement, the rep accepted it again and closed the call on a text follow-up for Monday.

objections.raw_quote: I still need, I still need that 24 hour period to think about this and sit down and actually run some numbers. I can't commit verbally right now until I do that.
objections.rep_response: Booked an informal follow-up: 'Why don't we touch base on Monday. I'll shoot you a text. Let me know what you're thinking.' No calendar hold, no scheduled call, no deposit offered, and no attempt to firm the payment plan he had just floated.

objections.raw_quote: with the travel, I haven't really sat down and figured out all the details and the costs of... I mean, I already know what El Salvador is going to be. We've done that once, but like Spain, and there could be a tack on to, you know, another two weeks, three weeks, who knows?
objections.rep_response: Explored it as a budgeting question and then repeatedly followed the prospect into surfing and travel tangents — Sardinia, the lost surfboard in Bogotá, what it feels like to catch a wave — rather than resolving how the programme survives four and a half months a year on the road. Never returned to it.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Floated but never specified. The rep first said 'We don't really have any set in stone payment plans or whatever, but I can at least give you a couple ideas', then 'If there was a way to break it down where we could fit it in month, like a month, more month-to-month basis'. When the prospect proposed $1,000 a month the rep answered 'I mean, yeah, I'd have to triple check. might be, because usually if we do a payment plan, they might bump it up a tiny bit.' No figure, term or uplift was ever stated.

prospect_financials.note: Deliberately vague. 'I've got money to cover everything' and he lived on the pension alone while still saving, but he declined the surplus question — 'I really don't look at it that way' — and no figures were obtained. Income streams are a UPS pension, newly started social security and a 401k. Committed and competing discretionary spend includes a just-ordered $2,200 custom surfboard, a booked Colorado trip, El Salvador, northern Spain and possible Barcelona and Sardinia extensions.

evidence: No payment, no link, no verbal agreement. The prospect refused explicitly: 'I couldn't do it right now. I still need that 24 hour period to think about this and sit down and actually run some numbers. I can't commit verbally right now until I do that.'
Rep closed on an informal text: 'Why don't we touch base on Monday. I'll shoot you a text. Let me know what you're thinking.' No call was booked and no calendar invite was mentioned.

Counter-evidence, positive: value was fully accepted and isolated as a non-issue — 'finances aside, like it does kind of check all the boxes for you... Correct?' answered 'Yeah. Oh yeah. That's not the issue', and 'I mean, I would absolutely love to do it. Yeah. But I just got to figure out how now.'

Counter-evidence, negative: the prospect has real competing commitments — a $2,200 custom board just ordered, a booked Colorado trip in August, El Salvador and Spain, with possible Barcelona and Sardinia extensions he will not know about for three weeks.

Structural counter-evidence: the prospect's own account undermines the need. He has trained consistently for 17 weeks unaided, walks 137 miles a month and self-rehabilitated a meniscus injury. He can demonstrably stick to things on his own, and the rep never addressed that.
outcome.next_step: Rep to text on Monday 2026-07-06. Prospect to run numbers within 24 hours and reconcile the $6,000 against booked and provisional travel. A monthly payment structure around $1,000 was raised as a possible unlock but was never confirmed or priced.

notable.note: Three things for a manager. First, the clinical picture: the prospect disclosed surgically treated atrial fibrillation and SVT with residual AFib, a surgically repaired Achilles with permanent calf atrophy, a shattered and repaired radius and an ongoing meniscus and knee problem — and the rep summarised all of it as 'it sounds like health-wise, injury-wise, sounds like there's nothing really to worry about, which is good', then sold loaded kettlebell work with no clinician clearance ever raised. Second, the rep does not know his own payment terms and said so on the call: 'We don't really have any set in stone payment plans or whatever' and 'we can be super flexible. Yeah. Not super flexible, but decently flexible.' Third, this call was inherited mid-pipeline — 'I'm taking over for Andrew, so my name's Michael, just as a heads up. Yeah, he had to step out' — which matters for how the outcome is attributed between reps. Also worth noting commercially: the prospect said 'All I care about is performance' and the rep sold him a six-pack four separate times.

quality.notes: Systematic and continuous inversion. The opening line under the rep's label is the prospect's, and the rep's own introduction — 'By the way, I'm taking over for Andrew, so my name's Michael' — sits under the prospect's label. The pattern holds throughout: nearly every discovery question, the entire three-pillar delivery and the $6,000 quote appear under whichever label the previous turn did not use. Around 00:21:00 a single block attributed to the prospect contains four alternating turns with no breaks. Roles resolved purely from content.
